Evidence shows budgets and spend monitoring exist as a feature (docs-16, docs-30) and a generic Vercel openapi.json exists (probe-3), but there is no evidence of an admin API specifically for programmatically creating gateways, API keys, or budgets — the documented flows describe dashboard/UI-based key and budget management, not a scriptable admin API.

The Gateway supports automatic failover, retries, and provider ordering/sorting (docs-3, docs-9, docs-10, docs-13) which can mitigate a single provider's rate limits by shifting traffic to others, and BYOK lets you pass different credentials per request (docs-27). However, there is no documented mechanism for spreading load across multiple keys for the same provider or for explicit request queuing/throttling to smooth rate limits.

Docs describe a Logs page with per-request detail (request ID, model, provider, status, routing) plus a Requests section with summaries by project/API key, and a Usage section tracking spend/tokens, directly matching the story's needs for latency, tokens, and cost visibility per request.

Docs confirm a caching feature (`caching: 'auto'` in providerOptions.gateway) that auto-applies provider caching strategies to reduce cost/latency, and community evidence shows discounted cache-read pricing on some models, corroborating real cost savings. However, this is provider-passthrough caching rather than a gateway-native full response cache, and there's no evidence of gateway-level dedup/caching for repeated identical requests across providers.

Vercel AI Gateway offers automatic failover to other providers on request failure (docs-3), per-provider timeouts for fast failover (docs-10), and BYOK fallback to system credentials on failure (docs-13), which functionally covers transient-error resilience. However, there is no explicit 'retry policy' configuration (e.g., retry counts, backoff, error-code filters) documented—only ordering/sorting of providers and automatic failover, so control over retry behavior is limited.

Docs show OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API and SDK compatibility across providers, which implies standard SSE streaming support (as used by OpenAI-compatible clients/AI SDK), but no evidence pack item explicitly documents or demonstrates token-by-token streaming behavior or tests it in practice.

The Gateway is OpenAI/Chat-Completions compatible and passes through provider-specific parameters (docs-7, docs-28), which implies structured/JSON-schema response formats could be forwarded, and tool-calling support is shown (docs-26). However, no evidence explicitly confirms guaranteed JSON-schema output normalization or validation across all providers.

Docs show OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API and unified schema across providers, with example tool/function-call usage (ToolLoopAgent with tools) using a single model string that can be swapped between providers (e.g., 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5'), enabling consistent tool-calling across providers via existing SDKs like OpenAI/AI SDK.

Vercel provides a built-in Logs page with search/filter and CSV/JSON export of request logs, plus a Usage/Requests dashboard, but there's no evidence of native trace export (e.g., OpenTelemetry) or direct integration with external observability stacks like Datadog/Grafana—only manual CSV/JSON export of filtered logs.

Vercel AI Gateway provides a single unified API (OpenAI-compatible) to access hundreds of models across many providers with minimal code changes, confirmed by docs and a live probe showing a working, OpenAI-compatible /v1/models endpoint listing multiple providers' models.

Docs show a single gateway API key abstracts away raw provider keys, and spend/budgets and request logs can be scoped per API key, project, or team member, implying support for issuing multiple scoped keys. However, there's no explicit documentation of a key-creation/rotation workflow or team/app-scoped key issuance API, so full key-management delivery isn't clearly evidenced.
